StackType.rationale: PowerStackType.Single and the sim does NOT override on_stack, so it adds -- which is what PowerCmd.ModifyAmount does (PowerCmd.cs:236). Nothing on either side reads Minion's Amount; it is a pure marker power. Faithful, and the correct handling of Single -- worth contrasting with the 15 units that override on_stack to `pass`.

OwnerIsSecondaryEnemy.maps_to: combat.py `primaries = [e for e in self.enemies if "minion" not in e.powers]`
OwnerIsSecondaryEnemy.rationale: C# reads it through Creature.IsSecondaryEnemy (`Creature.cs:276`, `Powers.Any(p => p.OwnerIsSecondaryEnemy)`); the sim tests the power id directly in `_all_enemies_dead` (combat.py), so combat is won once every PRIMARY enemy is gone. Same predicate, and the `or self.enemies` fallback correctly handles an all-minion board. Third-file citations, not hashed here.

ShouldPowerBeRemovedAfterOwnerDeath.rationale: `ShouldPowerBeRemovedAfterOwnerDeath() => false`. C# strips a dead creature's powers at CreatureCmd.cs:533 (`creature.RemoveAllPowersAfterDeath()`, then each power's AfterRemoved) and this override opts out so the power survives the death it is supposed to react to. The sim never removes powers on death at all -- a grep of cmds.py's kill/death path finds no `powers.clear()` or per-power removal, and cmds.py goes straight from the HP write to should_die / should_remove_from_combat_after_death / on_death -- so `false` is the sim's universal behaviour and this override is satisfied for free. Faithful HERE. The inverse is a real machinery gap owned by nobody: the C# DEFAULT is `true`, so every power WITHOUT this override should be stripped on its owner's death and in the sim none is. That is reported in content-power-report-b.md section 3 rather than verdicted on this unit, because it is an engine-wide absence and not this power's divergence. Third-file citations, not hashed here. ENGINE-LEVEL SIBLING (added 2026-07-26): the INVERSE finding -- that C#'s DEFAULT is `true` so every power WITHOUT this override should be stripped on its owner's death and in the sim none is -- now carries a verdict of its own at audit/records/seam/creature_card_cmds.json step 8b (`gap`, LIVE, executed on the Decimillipede). It used to exist only as prose in content-power-report-b.md section 3c. This entry stays `faithful` because the override asks for exactly the behaviour the sim gives for free; the engine-wide absence is step 8b's, not this unit's.

ShouldOwnerDeathTriggerFatal.issue: Closed 2026-07-29 (round 7): `PowerModel.ShouldOwnerDeathTriggerFatal` EXISTS in the sim now. `Power.should_owner_death_trigger_fatal` defaults to True (PowerModel.cs:646) and the two non-mock overrides are ported at their own sites -- MinionPower unconditionally (MinionPower.cs:20-23) and ReattachPower as `_all_others_down()` (ReattachPower.cs:106-109, whose own comment says "shouldn't trigger fatal unless all other segments are dead too"). `cmds.should_trigger_fatal(target)` is the `Target.Powers.All(...)` test, and BOTH Fatal cards call it BEFORE their attack, which is where C# reads it and is load-bearing: the killing blow strips the very powers the test asks about (Creature.RemoveAllPowersAfterDeath). This is NOT death prevention -- the minion really dies -- which is exactly why the `is_dead` check both cards already had did not cover it. MinionPower's override is the unconditional one. Its three ported appliers -- the Fabricator's bots, the Queen's minions and the Ovicopter's eggs -- are what made this live.  Pinned by test/test_card_residue_gaps.py.  NOT CLOSED: nothing at this site.  The text it replaced read: **LIVE.** C# reads this at three card sites -- `Feed.cs:38`, `HandOfGreed.cs:49`, `TheHunt.cs:41`, each `cardPlay.Target.Powers.All(p => p.ShouldOwnerDeathTriggerFatal())` computed BEFORE the attack -- and MinionPower returns **false**, so killing a minion never triggers a Fatal payoff. The sim has no such hook anywhere (`hooks.py` defines none) and `cards/feed.py` tests only `target.is_dead`. **EXECUTED**: Feed played into a 4-HP Tough Egg carrying MinionPower 1 raises the sim player's max HP from 80 to 83 (delta **3**) where the game raises it by **0**; the control -- the same egg without MinionPower -- gives delta 3 on both sides, so the divergence is the marker power and nothing else. Rule-6 co-occurrence: Feed is a ported Rare Ironclad Attack (cards/feed.py) and Tough Eggs receive MinionPower from the ported Act-2 Hive Ovicopter (monsters/hive/ovicopter.py, `PowerCmd.apply(ctx.hooks, egg, MinionPower, 1, applier=self)`), which lays up to five of them; the Kin Followers are a second ported source. Hand of Greed and The Hunt are unported, so Feed is the whole live surface today -- and it is enough. The fix is a `should_owner_death_trigger_fatal` hook plus one line in cards/feed.py, both outside audit scope. Third-file citations, not hashed here.
